info.name: Connectum: platform API reference
info.description:
# Connectum: platform API reference (for the mobile team)

Everything a mobile app needs to talk to the Connectum backend: how to reach it, how to sign in, the HTTP endpoints, the chat WebSocket and the `/sd` actions the web app uses. Sample responses were captured from a real running server.

## 1. Reaching the server (read this first)

The Connectum server runs on a **private IP address** (`10.0.2.146`). It is **not on the internet**. You can reach it in only two ways:

1. **From inside the office network**, or
2. **Through the WireGuard VPN** from anywhere else (home, mobile data, travel).

How to connect with WireGuard:
1. Install the **WireGuard** app (iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, Linux).
2. Ask the person who manages the VPN (IT / the backend owner) for your **WireGuard configuration** (a `.conf` file or QR code). It is personal: never share it or put it in a repository.
3. Import it into WireGuard and switch the tunnel **on**.
4. With the tunnel on, run **0. Check you can reach the server** in this collection. A JSON answer means you are connected. A timeout means the tunnel is off, or the profile is wrong.

Things to know:
- An app build that talks to this server also needs the tunnel on the phone, or the phone on the office Wi-Fi. A phone on ordinary mobile data without the VPN cannot reach it.
- The address works over plain `http` and `ws` today. A production address with `https` / `wss` will replace it; only the two variables below change.
- Sign-in codes are **emailed**; they do not appear in the API answer.

## 2. Quick start (5 minutes)

1. Be on the office network or switch the WireGuard tunnel on.
2. Open the collection **Variables** tab. Set `email` to **your own email address** (the one the backend owner invited, see section 5). Leave the others as they are: `baseUrl` = `http://10.0.2.146`, `wsUrl` = `ws://10.0.2.146/ws`.
3. Folder **1** > request **0** > Send. You should see `"platform": true`.
4. Folder **2** > **1. Ask for a sign-in code** > Send. A 6-digit code arrives in your email.
5. Type the code into the `otp` variable, then Send **2. Verify the code**. This saves your tokens and organisation for you.
6. Send **4. Enter an organisation**, then **5. Session**. You are in. Everything else in the collection now works.

## 3. How sign-in works

```
email --login/start--> code by email --login/verify--> identity token + organisations + remember-device token
identity token --enter (pick an organisation)--> session token
session token --> HTTP calls (Bearer) and the WebSocket handshake
```

- A person has **one account** (their email) and can belong to **many organisations**. The **identity token** is only for choosing, joining and entering organisations. The **session token** is what every other call uses and it belongs to one organisation.
- **Remember this device:** `login/verify` also returns `trust`. Keep it in the phone's secure storage and send it with the next `login/start`. If it is valid, the server skips the email code (about 15 days from the code that issued it). It is kept when the person signs out. A wrong or expired token simply gets a normal code.
- **Sessions last about 15 days and are not extended by use.** After that the WebSocket sends `session_expired` and closes; sign in again.
- A person waiting for approval (`status: pending`) cannot enter yet.

## 4. Answers and errors

Every HTTP answer is JSON. Success: `{"ok": true, "data": {...}}`. Failure: `{"ok": false, "error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "details": {...}}}`. Show `message` to the person; branch on `code`. Common codes: `invalid` (HTTP 400), `invalid_values` (a form field is wrong, `details.fields` says which), `unauthenticated` (401, no or bad token), `otp_invalid` (401, wrong or expired code), `forbidden` / `not_allowed` (403), `not_found` (404), `no_account` (404), `rate_limited` (429; wait and retry), `pending_approval`, `admin_locked`. Times are **epoch milliseconds** unless a field is a date string.

## 5. Getting an account to test with

Signing in needs a person who already exists in an organisation, and a real email address that can receive the code. Ask the backend owner to **invite your email address** into the test organisation (Admin console > Invite user). After you sign in once, that organisation appears in the answer of **2. Verify the code**. A person with no account can also create one (folder 3), but an administrator may still have to approve them before they can enter.

## 6. Notes for the mobile app (http, certificate, storage)

- **Use `http` and `ws` for now.** The server also answers on `https`, but its certificate is **self-signed**, so Postman (turn off *SSL certificate verification* in Settings) and a phone will refuse it. A proper `https` / `wss` address will come with production.
- **Plain http on a phone needs a setting.** iOS blocks it by default: add an App Transport Security exception for `10.0.2.146`. Android blocks cleartext by default: allow cleartext for that host in the network security config. Remove both when the production `https` address exists.
- **Store tokens in the secure storage** (iOS Keychain, Android Keystore): the session token and the remember-this-device token (`trust`). Never log them.
- **Keep the WebSocket alive:** reconnect with the same session token if it drops, and sign in again on `session_expired`. Expect a few seconds of delay on a slow VPN link: use a timeout of about 30 seconds for HTTP calls.
- **Sign-in codes are emailed** and last 5 minutes. There is no code in the API answer.

## 7. What is in this collection

| Folder | What |
|---|---|
| 1. Reach the server | One request to prove your connection works. |
| 2. Sign in | Code, verify, organisations, enter, session, sign out. |
| 3. New account and joining | Register, find an organisation, join. |
| 4. Feed and files (HTTP) | The workspace feed; uploading and downloading files. |
| 5. WebSocket: connect and chat | The handshake and every chat command and event (reference cards: see the note inside). |
| 6. WebSocket: actions (/sd) | The actions the app uses (about 130), by area: a card with a real sample for the common ones and a table for all of them. |

**Left out on purpose:** the administrator console, the Axpert ARM calls, the consumer program, the message queue and the Shopify calls. Those are for administrators and the server team, not the mobile app.

item.name: 1. Reach the server
item.description: Needs the WireGuard VPN or the office network. See the collection description.

item.name: 0. Check you can reach the server

request.description:
**Run this first.** It needs no sign-in.

- **You get `{"ok":true,"data":{"mode":"strict","platform":true}}`**: your network path works. You are on the office network or the WireGuard tunnel is on. Go on to folder 2.
- **It hangs and times out**: you are not connected. Switch the WireGuard tunnel on (or join the office Wi-Fi) and try again.
- **Certificate error**: you used `https`. The server's certificate is self-signed; use `http` for now (see the collection description, section 6).

This address serves several organisations, so it answers with platform information. An organisation's own details (branches, designations ...) come from "An organisation's public page" in folder 3.

item.name: 2. Sign in
item.description: Run in order: 1, 2, 3, 4. Steps 1 and 2 need no token; step 3 uses the identity token; step 4 gives the session token.

request.description:
Step 1 of signing in. The person types their email; Connectum emails a 6-digit code.

**`trust`** is optional: the remember-this-device token from an earlier `login/verify`. If it is valid (about 15 days from the code that issued it, kept even after signing out), the server skips the code and answers with the signed-in result straight away (`trusted: true`, token and organisations), so the next call is `enter`. Send an empty or missing `trust` the first time.

No account for that email gives `no_account`. Too many tries gives `rate_limited` (HTTP 429).

response.name: 200 OK, remembered device: signed in at once
404 no account for that email

request.description:
Step 2. Put the 6-digit code from the email into the **`otp` variable** (collection > Variables), or type it in the body below, then send. Send it within 5 minutes. On success you get the **identity token** (`token`), the person's account (`identity`) and the list of organisations they belong to (`enterprises`), plus **`trust`**, the remember-this-device token. Store `trust` securely on the phone (keychain/keystore) and send it with the next `login/start`.

The identity token is only for picking, joining and entering organisations. It is **not** the token the chat uses: call `enter` for that.

`deviceId` is any stable id for this install.

response.name: 401 wrong or expired code

exec: if (j.ok && j.data && j.data.enterprises && j.data.enterprises.length) { const a = j.data.enterprises.find(e => e.status === "active") || j.data.enterprises[0]; pm.collectionVariables.set("enterprise", a.enterprise); }

request.description: Who is this account and which organisations is it in? Use the identity token. `status` is `active`, or `pending` while an administrator still has to approve the person.

item.name: 4. Enter an organisation (get the session token)

request.description:
Pick one organisation from `enterprises` and enter it. The previous step already saved the first active organisation into the `enterprise` variable, so just press Send. The answer holds the **session token** (`token`): use it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` for every other HTTP call and in the WebSocket handshake. It lasts about 15 days and is **not** extended by activity; when it ends the socket receives `session_expired` and the person signs in again (usually with the remembered device, so no code).

`user` is the person's profile inside this organisation. Errors: `pending_approval`, `rejected`, `account_inactive`, `not_member`.

item.name: 5. WebSocket: connect and chat
item.description: Postman cannot store WebSocket requests, so these are reference cards. Open a WebSocket request to `{{wsUrl}}` to try them.

item.name: WS · How to connect (read this first)

request.description:
**These cards document WebSocket messages.** Postman collections cannot hold WebSocket requests, so each card is a harmless `GET /api/sd/session` (it only proves your token works). The text and the saved examples are the reference. To really try a message use Postman's own **New > WebSocket** request.

**1. Open** `{{wsUrl}}` (for example `ws://10.0.2.146/ws`).

**2. First frame must be JSON:** `{"username":"asha","token":"<session token>","armSessionId":"any-text"}`. `username` is the person's username in this organisation, **in lower case** (a name in capitals is refused: "That session belongs to a different username"; max 24 characters, no spaces); `token` is the **session token** from `enter`. `armSessionId` is optional and not used.

**3. The server answers** `{"type":"welcome","name":"asha"}` followed by a `history` event for the global room. A bad token or username gives `{"type":"error","text":"..."}`.

**4. After that, every frame you SEND is plain text**, one command per frame (`/msg ravi hello`, `/history dm ravi`, `/sd me {}`). **Every frame you RECEIVE is JSON** with a `type`.

**Actions:** `/sd <action> {json}` runs one of the actions in folder 6. Put a `reqId` of your own in the JSON; it is echoed in the reply `{"type":"sd","reqId":...,"ok":true,"data":{...}}` or `{"ok":false,"error":{"code","message","details?"}}`. Server-pushed changes arrive as `{"type":"sd_event","event":"...","data":{...}}`.

**Limits:** a message is at most 2000 characters; commands are rate limited (a limited command still gets a reply). The session ends after about 15 days (`session_expired` event, then the socket closes). One live connection per person. **Reconnecting** with the same session takes the old socket over at once (no waiting time, no "Username taken"): the old socket gets `{"type":"sd_event","event":"connection_superseded","reason":"opened_elsewhere"}` and is closed. A fresh **sign-in** on another device ends the old session instead (`session_replaced`, `signed_in_elsewhere`).

`/list` gives the usernames that are online now.

**You send:** `/list`

`/msg <username> <text>`. In strict mode you can only message an administrator and people you are connected with; otherwise you get an `error` with code `not_associated`. `status` is `delivered` (they are online) or `queued` (stored for when they connect).

**You send:** `/msg ravi Hello Ravi, are you on rounds today?`

Pushed by the server when someone messages you. Same shape as a global `chat` event.

Also pushed: `typing_dm`, `dm_read`, `dm_reaction`, `dm_deleted`, `profile`, `added_to_group`, `group_message`, `link_preview` and more (list in the description of the next cards).

response.name: private event
response.body:
{
 "type": "private",
 "id": 1,
 "ts": 1793166707278,
 "from": "asha",
 "text": "Hello Ravi, are you on rounds today?",
 "replyTo": null
}

request.description:
`/history dm <username>` returns up to the last 50 messages, oldest first. Also `/history group <name>` and `/history host <hostKey>`. `ts` is epoch milliseconds.

**You send:** `/history dm ravi`

response.name: What you receive
response.body:
{
 "type": "history",
 "scope": "dm",
 "with": "ravi",
 "now": 1793166707302,
 "list": [
  {
   "id": 1,
   "ts": 1793166707278,
   "from": "asha",
   "text": "Hello Ravi, are you on rounds today?",
   "kind": "chat",
   "private": true,
   "reactions": [],
   "deleted": false,
   "editedTs": null,
   "replyTo": null,
   "previewUrl": "",
   "previewTitle": "",
   "previewDescription": "",
   "previewImage": ""
  }
 ]
}

item.name: WS · Send with a client id (no double sends)

request.description:
`/c <clientId> <command>` runs the command as usual and echoes your id in the ack as `cid`. If the connection drops and you send the **same id again**, nothing is sent twice: you get the first ack back with `duplicate: true`. The id is remembered for one day, per person. Works for `/msg`, `/replydm`, `/groupmsg`, `/replygroup`, `/hostmsg`. It does not work for plain messages to the global room (`cid_unsupported`). The id is 1 to 64 characters: letters, digits and `- _ . :` (else `bad_cid`). A refused send is not remembered, so you can retry with the same id.

**You send:** `/c 7f3a-0001 /msg ravi Hello Ravi`

`/history dm <username> before <messageId>` gives up to 50 messages older than that id, oldest first. Ask with the oldest id you hold. `hasMore` says whether still older ones exist; `next` is the id to ask with next (`null` when the page is empty). Also works for `group <name>` and `host <hostKey>`. A conversation the person cleared stays cleared. A `before` without a number gives an `error` with code `usage`.

**You send:** `/history dm ravi before 1790071256909`

response.name: What you receive
response.body:
{
 "type": "history",
 "scope": "dm",
 "with": "ravi",
 "now": 1790071300000,
 "before": 1790071256909,
 "hasMore": true,
 "next": 1790070000000,
 "list": [
  "... up to 50 messages, each shaped like in 'Direct message history' ..."
 ]
}

item.name: WS · Is a message encrypted? (e2e flag)

request.description: A message whose text is an end-to-end encrypted envelope (`e2e1:...`) carries `e2e: true` in `history` and in the `/conversations` list. Plain messages have no `e2e` field. The organisation-wide mode (off, optional, required) is `e2e.status` in folder 6.

`/conversations` lists every direct-message thread, newest first, with its last message. This is how the app learns who wrote while it was offline.

**You send:** `/conversations`

`/creategroup <name>`: at most 32 characters, no spaces (use `ward_round`). You become the owner. Add people with `/addmember <group> <username>`; leave with `/leavegroup <group>`.

**You send:** `/creategroup ward_round`

`/groupmsg <group> <text>`. Members receive a `group_message` event.

**You send:** `/groupmsg ward_round Round starts at 10`

`/groups` lists the groups you are in.

**You send:** `/groups`

`/typing dm <username>` (or `group <name>`, or `global`). No reply; the other person receives `typing_dm`.

**You send:** `/typing dm ravi`

`/getprofile <username>` returns their avatar and status. Set your own with `/setstatus <text>`, `/setavatar <url>`, `/removeavatar`.

**You send:** `/getprofile ravi`

Commands that are refused or malformed come back as `error` with a human `text` and sometimes a `code` (`not_associated`, `not_allowed`, `usage`, `unknown_command`).

**You send:** `/nope`

response.name: What you receive

item.name: WS · Presence (someone went online or offline)

request.description: Sent by the server to a person who knows them (connected to them, or who could message them): `{"type":"presence","user":"ravi","online":false,"ts":...}`. Use `/list` once when the app starts or resumes, then follow `presence`. A reconnect that takes over a live connection sends none.

item.name: WS · Receipt (the other person received or read your messages)

request.description: Sent to the sender of a direct conversation when the other person calls `conv.delivered` or `conv.read` (or the old `/read dm <user>`). It is also KEPT: read `peerReadId` / `peerDeliveredId` from `conv.list` with `full:true`, so a person who was offline still learns it. In a group the author asks `conv.readers`.

`/read group <name>` keeps the read position of a group (like `/read dm <user>` for a direct conversation, or `conv.read` with an id). No reply.

**You send:** `/read group ward_a`

| You send | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/react dm <username> <messageId> <emoji>` | Toggle a reaction (also `group <name>`, `global`). |
| `/delete dm <username> <messageId>` | Delete your own message (also `group`, `global`). |
| `/replydm <username> <messageId> <text>` | Reply inside a DM (also `/replygroup`). |
| `/read dm <username>` | Mark a thread read; the other person gets `dm_read`. |
| `/addmember <group> <username>` | Add someone to a group you are in. |
| `/leavegroup <group>` | Leave a group. |
| `/gifsearch [query]`, `/stickersearch [query]` | Search GIFs or stickers. |
| `/cmds [prefix]` | The `#command` catalog; `#dm alice hi` style shortcuts run the matching `/command`. |
| `/quit` | Clean disconnect. |

Events you may receive: `chat`, `private`, `system`, `group_message`, `group_system`, `added_to_group`, `typing`, `typing_dm`, `group_typing`, `dm_ack`, `dm_read`, `group_msg_ack`, `reaction`, `dm_reaction`, `group_reaction`, `profile`, `deleted`, `dm_deleted`, `group_deleted`, `delete_denied`, `link_preview`, `error`, and `sd_event` (organisation changes such as `notifications_changed`, `permissions_changed`, `session_expired`).

item.name: 6. WebSocket: actions (/sd)
item.description: Every action is the text frame `/sd <action> {json}` on the WebSocket.

item.name: Session and profile (14)
item.description:
The actions the app uses in this area (14). Each one is a WebSocket message: `/sd <action> {json}`. The table lists every action with its arguments and reply shape. The cards below are real examples captured from a running test hospital (long lists are cut to one item).

| Action | Arguments | Reply | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `me` | `{}` | `{user, mode, feed, ...}` | Who the connection is: the signed-in user, the mode (open or strict) and counters. Works on any open connection. |
| `profile.get` | `{}` | `{profile}` | Everything about me: address, gender, date of birth, education, skills, roles. |
| `profile.update` | `{address?, gender?, dob?, education?, skills?, city?, country?, pin?}` | `{profile}` | Change my own profile. Nothing else can be changed here. |
| `settings.get` | `{}` | `{settings:{themeMode, globalChatColorId, chatColorOverrides, liquidGlass, updated}}` | My saved theme and chat colours (kept on the server so every device agrees). |
| `settings.save` | `{themeMode?, globalChatColorId?, chatColorOverrides?, liquidGlass?}` | `{settings}` | Save settings. Only what is sent changes. |
| `permissions.mine` | `{}` | `{permissions, known, onboardsEmployees, canInviteEmployees}` | What my roles allow (broadcast, register affiliates, invite customers/suppliers) and whether I may invite employees. |
| `connect.my` | `{}` | `{person:{code, display, payload, url, name, username}, enterprise:{...card...}}` | My personal connect code (for the QR) and the enterprise card. |
| `connect.rotate` | `{}` | `{person}` | A new personal code; the old one stops working. |
| `connect.scan` | `{code}` | `{associated \| enterprise}` | Scan a code. A personal code makes the two of you associates at once; an enterprise code returns its card. |
| `e2e.status` | `{}` | `{mode, devices, maxDevices}` | End-to-end encryption: the mode and which of my devices are registered. |
| `e2e.register` | `{id (32 hex), ecdh, sign, proof, label?}` | `{device}` | Register this device: its ECDH and signing public keys (P-256, base64url) and the proof of the signing key. 30 registrations an hour. |
| `e2e.remove` | `{id}` | `{removed}` | Remove one of my device keys. |
| `e2e.devices` | `{users:[usernames] (1..50)}` | `{devices:{username:[device]}}` | The public device keys of the people I may message (to encrypt a direct message to them). |
| `e2e.group_devices` | `{group}` | `{members:[{user, devices}]}` | The device keys of every member of a group. |

request.description:
**Send:** `/sd me {}`  (add a `reqId` of your own to the JSON)

**Arguments:** `{}`

Who the connection is: the signed-in user, the mode (open or strict) and counters. Works on any open connection.

item.name: People, hosts and connections (17)
item.description:
The actions the app uses in this area (17). Each one is a WebSocket message: `/sd <action> {json}`. The table lists every action with its arguments and reply shape. The cards below are real examples captured from a running test hospital (long lists are cut to one item).

| Action | Arguments | Reply | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `assoc.list` | `{}` | `{associates:[{user, relation: host\|user\|peer, online}]}` | My contact list: the people I am connected to, and what they are to me. |
| `assoc.invite` | `{to}` | `{request}` | Ask someone to connect (a peer link). They must accept. |
| `assoc.handover` | `{person, to}` | `{request}` | Employees/admins: hand a person I am connected with (a patient, a customer) over to another employee. The person is asked first. |
| `users.search` | `{q}` | `{users:[{username, name, designation, designations, department, branch, affiliate, category, isEmployee, isHost, status, canInteract, connected, canMessage, avatar}]}` | Find people (at most 20; not yourself, not deactivated people). Strict mode: exact username, email or mobile only. canInteract: the interaction rules allow it; connected: already linked; canMessage: a direct message would be accepted now; avatar: the picture address or null. |
| `users.invite` | `{name, email, mobile?, isEmployee?, branch?, department?, designation?, designations?, reportingManager?, employeeCode?, category?, roles?, isHost?, hostScope?}` | `{user}` | Invite one person. Administrators and hosts invite anyone in their scope; an employee whose designation may onboard invites those employees; a role may allow inviting customers/suppliers. |
| `users.resend_invite` | `{username}` | `{sent, to}` | Send the invitation again to someone who has not signed in yet (once a minute). |
| `req.list` | `{status?, limit?, offset?}` | `{requests, total, offset, limit, hasMore}` | My requests: approvals to answer, connection requests, handovers. Default status is pending; `all` or a status. |
| `req.respond` | `{id, action: accept\|reject\|ignore, reason?, allowResubmit?}` | `{request}` | Answer a request. Declining a submission can allow the author to fix and resend it. |
| `forms.forward` | `{id, chats:[chat id]}` | `{results}` | Forward a submitted form (as a message) into other conversations. |
| `affiliate.register` | `{name, category, country?, city?, pin?, branches?}` | `{affiliate}` | Register an affiliate organisation (needs the register_affiliate role permission). Gets a number like AFF-000001. |
| `affiliate.list` | `{q?}` | `{affiliates:[{name, number, category, city, country}]}` | Employees: search affiliates. |
| `conv.list` | `{full?}` | `{conversations:[...]}` | {}: the conversations I have a state for (archived, deleted, pinned, muted, read). {full:true}: EVERY conversation (direct, groups, general room) with lastId, readId, unread (at most 99, unreadMore), pinned, muted, and for a direct one peerReadId, peerDeliveredId and the other person's avatar. |
| `conv.pin` | `{id}` | `{conversation}` | Pin a conversation for me (kept on the server). Idempotent. conv.unpin undoes it. |
| `conv.mute` | `{id}` | `{conversation}` | Mute a conversation for me (a flag: the app decides what quiet means). Idempotent. conv.unmute undoes it. |
| `conv.read` | `{id, upTo?}` | `{conversation}` | I have read up to that message (default: everything now). Only moves forward, clamped to the newest. The other person of a direct conversation gets a receipt event and later reads peerReadId. |
| `conv.delivered` | `{id, upTo?}` | `{conversation}` | My device has received up to that message (the sender's delivery tick). Reading implies it. |
| `conv.readers` | `{id:"group:<name>", messageId}` | `{messageId, total, readCount, readers:[{user, readTs}]}` | Who of the group has read my message. Only its author may ask. |

item.name: Forms, records and options (26)
item.description:
The actions the app uses in this area (26). Each one is a WebSocket message: `/sd <action> {json}`. The table lists every action with its arguments and reply shape. The cards below are real examples captured from a running test hospital (long lists are cut to one item).

| Action | Arguments | Reply | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `options.list` | `{}` | `{options:[{id, caption, type, category, target, targetScope, display, order, owner}]}` | The options I may see (an option's 'applicable to' rules decide). These are the Smart Prompts. |
| `options.categories` | `{}` | `{categories:[{id, label, icon, types, executable, count}], total}` | One entry per Smart Prompts pill, with how many options I have in it. |
| `option.run` | `{id, ...}` | `{open \| url \| ...}` | Run an option: open a form, an Axpert item, the catalog, start a payment ... The reply says what the app should do. not_configured when the option has nothing to open. |
| `tstruct.get` | `{name}` | `{tstruct}` | A form definition, if one of my options points at it. Fields with a `source` come with the current names as `options`. |
| `tstruct.submit` | `{name, values:{field: value}, ref?, meta?, cid?}` | `{submission, recordStatus, cid?, duplicate?}` | Fill in a form. cid (a client id, 1 to 64 characters: letters, digits, - _ . :) makes a retry safe: the same id again returns the first answer with duplicate:true and saves nothing (remembered a day, per person). recordStatus is saved, or pending when it needs approval. Setup forms also make the real change (result on the submission). |
| `submissions.list` | `{tstruct?, ref?, recordsOnly?, limit?, offset?}` | `{submissions, total, offset, limit, hasMore}` | My submissions plus those of the people I host. |
| `submission.get` | `{id}` | `{submission}` | One submission I may open (author, host, admin, an approver, a notified designation). |
| `submissions.update` | `{id, values?, meta?}` | `{submission}` | The author edits a submission (not while it waits for approval). Re-checked against the form; Auto Generate numbers are kept. |
| `submission.resubmit` | `{id, values?, meta?}` | `{submission}` | The author fixes a declined submission (if the approver allowed it) and sends it again. |
| `submissions.delete` | `{id}` | `{deleted}` | The author deletes a submission. |
| `tstruct.user.list` | `{}` | `{tstructs}` | Forms people made themselves (visible to everyone). |
| `tstruct.user.get` | `{name}` | `{tstruct}` | One user-made form. |
| `tstruct.user.save` | `{name, caption?, description?, fields[], sections[], approval?, notify?, saveToDb?, axpert?}` | `{tstruct}` | Create a form of my own. `duplicate` if the name is taken. An Axpert target is checked with MY Axpert connection. |
| `tstruct.user.update` | `{same body}` | `{tstruct}` | Edit my form (creator only). |
| `tstruct.user.delete` | `{name}` | `{deleted}` | Delete my form (creator only). Records are kept. |
| `tstruct.user.submit` | `{name, values, ref?, meta?}` | `{submission}` | Fill in a user-made form. |
| `option.user.list` | `{}` | `{options, types}` | The options I made (an administrator gets all). |
| `option.user.save` | `{id?, caption, type, target?, display?, applicable?, active?, order?}` | `{option}` | Create or edit an option of my own. |
| `option.user.delete` | `{id}` | `{deleted}` | Delete one (creator or administrator). |
| `cfg.lookups` | `{}` | `{branches, departments, designations, roles, categories, ...}` | The organisation's lists as names, for pickers (any signed-in person). |
| `care.names` | `{}` | `{...}` | The shared-thread titles for the person's care threads. |
| `care.summary` | `{person}` | `{...}` | The data for a summary of a person's shared thread. |
| `avail.get` | `{user?}` | `{...}` | Working hours of a person (or anything that can be booked): days, times, slot length, days off. |
| `avail.set` | `{user?, slotMinutes, advanceDays, week, off}` | `{...}` | Set working hours. |
| `avail.slots` | `{user, from?, days?}` | `{...}` | The free bookable times of a person for the next days. |

item.name: WS · /sd tstruct.submit with a client id (a retry never saves twice)

request.description:
Add `cid` (1 to 64 characters: letters, digits, - _ . :) to a save. If the connection drops and you send the **same cid again**, nothing is saved twice: you get the first answer back with `duplicate: true`. The id is remembered a day, per person. Works for `tstruct.submit`, `tstruct.user.submit`, `submissions.update` and `submission.resubmit`. A save that was refused is not remembered, so you can retry with the same cid. Two calls with the same cid at the same instant: one saves, the other gets `in_progress` (try again).

**You send:** `/sd tstruct.submit {"name":"orders","values":{"item":"Pen","qty":2},"cid":"7f3a-0001"}`

item.name: Applications, data sources, links and AI (23)
item.description:
The actions the app uses in this area (23). Each one is a WebSocket message: `/sd <action> {json}`. The table lists every action with its arguments and reply shape. The cards below are real examples captured from a running test hospital (long lists are cut to one item).

| Action | Arguments | Reply | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `applications.list` | `{}` | `{applications:[{name, commandLine, axpert, ...}]}` | The applications connected to this organisation (names only: no addresses or credentials). |
| `datasource.list` | `{}` | `{datasources}` | The data sources I may use: admin-made ones that apply to me, plus my own. |
| `datasource.save` | `{name, type: sql\|api\|appsource, connection, sql \| path+method \| appSource+runAs, params:[{name, default}], columns?, description?, cacheSec?, applicable?}` | `{datasource}` | Create or edit. sql = one read-only SELECT; api = a path on the connection; appsource = an Axpert application's own data source (admin only). |
| `datasource.delete` | `{name}` | `{deleted}` | Delete one (blocked while a global variable reads from it). |
| `datasource.run` | `{name, values, limit} \| {tstruct, field, scope?, values}` | `{columns, rows, total, truncated}` | Run a data source (slow). With tstruct+field it runs the source that form field names, through the form (people filling the form need no access to the source). |
| `globals.list` | `{}` | `{builtins, custom, values}` | The global variables and my values. |
| `globals.resolve` | `{}` | `{values}` | My values, including those a data source supplies (slow). |
| `shopify.products` | `{q?, cursor?}` | `{items:[{id, title, handle, vendor, image, priceMin, priceMax, currency, available, url}], pageInfo:{hasNext, cursor}, shop:{name}}` | Active products of the connected store, 24 a page, cached 2 minutes. not_configured when no store is connected. |
| `ai.enterprise` | `{...}` | `{...}` | What the assistant may read of the organisation, always as the person asking: the forms they may open, and (administrators only) the people directory. |
| `ai.conv.list` | `{limit?, before?, q?}` | `{...}` | The person's saved AI conversations: pinned first, the rest by day, paged, searchable. |
| `ai.conv.pin` | `{id, pinned}` | `{...}` | Pin or unpin an AI conversation. |
| `ai.conv.get` | `{id}` | `{...}` | Open a saved AI conversation (messages are sealed at rest). |
| `ai.conv.save` | `{id?, title?, messages, ...}` | `{...}` | Save an AI conversation so it can be opened from any device. |
| `ai.conv.rename` | `{id, title}` | `{...}` | Rename an AI conversation. |
| `ai.conv.delete` | `{id}` | `{...}` | Delete a saved AI conversation. |
| `ai.agents` | `{}` | `{...}` | The AI agents this person may use: {agents:[{id, name, alias, provider, model}]}. |
| `ai.models` | `{agent, refresh?}` | `{...}` | The models this agent's key can use, so a person picks only what the plan allows (slow lane). |
| `api.list` | `{}` | `{...}` | The API plugins described for a form builder (names, kind, parameters, columns; no secrets). |
| `api.run` | `{name, values?, tstruct?, field?, ...}` | `{...}` | Run an API plugin (the data source of a form field) as the person, through the form (slow lane; 120 calls a minute). |

item.name: Axpert connection (optional) (8)
item.description:
The actions the app uses in this area (8). Each one is a WebSocket message: `/sd <action> {json}`. The table lists every action with its arguments and reply shape. The cards below are real examples captured from a running test hospital (long lists are cut to one item).

| Action | Arguments | Reply | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `axpert.status` | `{}` | `{connected, connections:[{app, username, sessionActive, remembered}], apps:[{name, frame}], access, canApprove}` | My Axpert connections and the applications I may connect to. Never a password, token or session id. |
| `axpert.request` | `{note?}` | `{status}` | Ask the administrators (or my manager) for Axpert access. Managers and HR need no approval. |
| `axpert.requests` | `{}` | `{requests:[{username, name, state, note, ts, by}]}` | Requests I may decide: everyone for an administrator, my team for a manager. |
| `axpert.decide` | `{username, decision: approve\|deny\|revoke}` | `{state}` | Decide a request (administrator, or the person's manager). |
| `axpert.connect` | `{app, username, password, remember?}` | `{status}` | Sign in to Axpert (slow). The sign-in is kept sealed by default, so the person never types it again. |
| `axpert.disconnect` | `{app?}` | `{status}` | Disconnect (every application when app is omitted). |
| `axpert.menu` | `{app?, refresh?}` | `{app, items:[{id, caption, type, target, group?}], shape}` | My Axpert menu (slow): tstructs, iviews and pages, cached 5 minutes. |
| `axpert.open` | `{app?, id}` | `{url, title, type, frame}` | The address of Axpert's own screen for a menu item (slow), to open in a pop-up or frame. |
